defects: Drops the lattice-specific setting entirely: no `Lattice X` / `JordanHolderLattice X` structure, so there is no notion of intervals, meet, join, or maximality involved

The 'moves' relation is left as an arbitrary free parameter `moves : α → α → Prop` instead of being fixed to the specific second-isomorphism-theorem relation (x, x ⊔ y) ~ (x ⊓ y, y) for IsMaximal x (x ⊔ y)

The target relation 'Iso' (the Jordan-Hölder isomorphism-of-intervals relation) is entirely absent; the conclusion instead uses the generic `Relation.EqvGen moves`, with no claim connecting EqvGen of the specific moves to Iso

As stated, the theorem reduces to a generic/trivial fact about equivalence closures (EqvGen is the least equivalence relation containing a relation) that holds for any relation on any type, not a statement specific to lattices or the second isomorphism theorem
Loses the informal statement's core content that the generating moves are indexed by a maximality condition (IsMaximal) tied to join/meet operations
